6. Wildlife
6.1 Issues:
Moose habitat has been marginalized by the mine operations and the Shulla Flats area has 
been identified as critical moose winter range. Ensuring that this habitat remains viable will be 
important to maintain the moose population in this area. Since there are high densities of 
ungulates using this area any decrease in browse could impact ungulate fitness or productivity.
Beavers can be adversely impacted by winter and spring thaws which raise the water levels 
and flood out beaver colonies at a time where there is nowhere else to go, resulting in mass 
drowning or migration out of the system.
Discharge rates to Witches Brook should attempt to mimic the seasonal hydrograph so that 
seasonal flooding and drying cycles better duplicate natural conditions which will allow the 
optimum growth of riparian vegetation that requires wet/dry cycle conditions to reproduce and 
flourish. 
A review of the provincial Conservation Data Centre’s database found no records of rare or 
endangered vertebrates or invertebrates. In the short term there will be a minor overall negative 
impact to birds utilizing riparian shrublands although it is anticipated that marsh species may 
increase as marsh habitats increase in size. After four years following initiation it is anticipated 
there will be overall positive impacts to bird fauna along Witches Brook and Guichon Creek. 
The greatest longterm impact will be to bird communities using recently created grasslands. 
Implementation of discharge initiation outside the breeding period of birds will assist in assuring 
that impacts to nests and nestlings are avoided.
6.2 Assessment of Issues:
The Ministries are satisfied that the proponent has committed to the following mitigation 
measures to address potential impacts to wildlife and wildlife habitat:
●     Planting to replace short term losses in moose browse in Shulla Flats focussing on 
planting of live stakes of browse species – over the long-term it is estimated that browse 
should increase if other mitigation measures such as those listed below are 
implemented;
●     Working with stakeholders to develop a Range Use Plan to minimize cattle impacts on 
newly planted moose browse in the Shulla Flat area;
●     Monitoring moose browse along Witches Brook and Guichon Creek in September of 
each year there is an increase in groundwater discharge. If die-back has occurred, a 
planting program will be implemented.

7. Adaptive Management and the Technical Coordinating Committee 
7.1 Issues:
As much of the information presented in the project application is based on various modelling 
exercises, an adaptive management approach to this project will be needed to ensure that 
appropriate actions are taken if monitoring data or information indicates adverse impacts 
occurring. The data and information collected through the various proposed monitoring 
programs should be used to adjust the modelled results on a continual basis in order to track 
any impacts on the resources in Witches Brook and Guichon Creek. In addition, monitoring 
results should be used to adjust mitigation measures where appropriate.
7.2 Assessment of Issues:
The Ministries support the use of an adaptive management approach to identifying and 
mitigating impacts from the project. A key component of this adaptive management strategy will 
be the formation of a Technical Coordinating Committee formed from representatives from 
Highland Valley Copper, federal and provincial agencies, local governments, First Nations, and 
the Guichon Creek Water User Community and the agricultural community. The proponent will 
be responsible for performing the monitoring and reporting to the committee. Monitoring results 
will be used to adjust the discharges and adjust the scope and frequency of monitoring as 
needed.
7.3 Recommendations:
It will be important that the proposed coordinating committee be functioning prior to project 
approval. In order to facilitate this it is recommended that the following be provided by the 
proponent prior to project approval for review by the relevant agencies:
●     Draft terms of reference for the proposed coordinating committee including a dispute 
resolution process; and 
●     A summary list of commitments made by the proponent in the project application and 
appendices.
As impacts of concern related to this project are linked to mine closure, it is the Ministries 
recommendation that the Technical Coordinating Committee be closely involved in the mine 
closure plans.
